Rashi on Niddah 20b:10:1.hebrew: בין טמאה לטהורה - כשכלין ימי טוהר של זכר או של נקבה, וראתה ביום ארבעים ואחד או ביום שמונים ואחד:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:10:1.english: Between an impure [woman] and a pure [woman] - When the days of purity for a male or for a female end, and she sees [blood] on the forty-first day or on the eighty-first day.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:10:2.hebrew: חזינא לההוא דמא - אי דם טמא מטמינא, ואי לאו מחמשה דמים הוא מטהרינא. דההוא ודאי טיפתא קמייתא מייתא, דלא מזהמא, דעד השתא חזאי ואתא דם טוהר, שכל מ' לזכר ופ' לנקבה מעין פתוח. ואפי' פסקה יום או יומים, הואיל ומוחזקת היא בדמים, לא זהמא ומייתא טיפתא קמייתא:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:10:2.english: I examine that blood - If [it is] impure blood, I declare [her] impure; and if it is not of the five [impure types of] blood, I declare [her] pure. For in that case, she certainly brings the first drop, as it is not foul, since until now she was seeing [blood] and pure blood had been flowing — for all forty [days] for a male and eighty for a female, the fountain is open. And even if [the bleeding] ceased for a day or two, since she is presumed to discharge blood, it is not foul, and she brings the first drop.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:13:1.english: Initially he deemed her impure - Rav Yitzḥak [did so] out of respect for Rabba bar Bar Ḥana.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:14:1.hebrew: כזה ראיתי - מביאה דם אחר, או שלה או של חברתה, ואומרת: כזה ראיתי ואבדתיו. אם דם זה טהור, לא מספקינן ליה בטומאה משום דם האבוד, דמהימנא למימר כזה ראיתי:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:14:1.english: I saw [blood] like this - She brings another [sample of] blood, either her own or her friend's, and says: "I saw [blood] like this, and I lost it." If this blood is pure, we do not hold it in doubt of impurity on account of the lost blood, as she is believed to say: "I saw [blood] like this."

Rashi on Niddah 20b:15:1.hebrew: כזה טיהר לי פלוני כו' מהו - שתסמוך עליה חברתה, שהראתה דמה לזו, ואמרה לה: כדם זה שלך הראתי גם אני לפלוני חכם, וטיהר:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:15:1.english: "So-and-so declared [blood] like this pure for me," etc., what is [the halakha]? - [The question is whether] her friend may rely upon her, where [the friend] showed her blood to this [woman] and [the latter] said to her: "Blood like this of yours, I too showed to so-and-so the sage, and he declared [it] pure."

Rashi on Niddah 20b:16:1.english: A woman is believed, etc. - Evidently, she is knowledgeable about the appearance of blood.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:16:2.hebrew: דליתיה קמן - אבל הכא דאיתיה קמן, ניחזי אנן:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:16:2.english: Since it is not before us - But here, since it is before us, let us examine [it] ourselves.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:19:1.hebrew: אגמריה סמך - דפשיטא ליה דטהור, והאי דהוה מטמא מעיקרא משום כבודו דרבה בר בר חנה, אבל אי הוה מספקא ליה, לא הוה סמיך עלה:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:19:1.english: He relied on his studies - For it was obvious to him that [the blood] was pure, and the fact that he initially declared [it] impure was out of deference to Rabba bar bar Ḥana; but had he been in doubt about it, he would not have relied upon her.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:1:1.english: For it is Rabbi Ḥanina who is wise - And is able to examine [blood] in this manner.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:20:1.english: He saw during the day - [This refers] to that very same blood.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:20:2.hebrew: חזר וטימא - קס"ד דלא חזר וראהו, אלא מאליו חזר בו וטימא, דסבר שמא אמש טמא הוה, ועכשיו שיבש נשתנה ממראיתו ממה שהיה לו אמש, ואילו הוה לח כמתחלתו הוה נראה טמא, לפיכך חזר בו ממה שטיהר:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:20:2.english: He again deemed it impure - The Gemara initially thought that he did not examine it again, but rather of his own accord he retracted and deemed it impure, for he reasoned that perhaps last night it was impure, and now that it has dried, its appearance has changed from what it had last night, and if it were moist as it was initially, it would appear impure; therefore, he retracted what he had deemed pure.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:20:3.hebrew: שמא טעיתי - במה שחזרתי וטימאתי, הואיל ומראיהו עכשיו טהור:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:20:3.english: Perhaps I erred - In that I retracted and deemed [it] impure, since its appearance now is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:22:1.hebrew: מעיקרא אחזקיה בטומאה - כלומר, אמש לא מספק טימא, אלא שפיר חזייה ואחזיק בטומאה, דאמרי' לקמן: רבי בדק לאור הנר:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:22:1.english: Initially, he established it as impure - That is to say, last night he did not deem it impure out of doubt, but rather he saw it well and established it as impure, as we say below: "Rabbi would examine [blood] by candlelight."

Rashi on Niddah 20b:22:2.english: That it changed - It turned white.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:22:3.english: That it changed again - Even more.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:22:4.hebrew: מפכח - מראה אדמומיתו עוברת, הילכך הדר למילתיה קמייתא וטימא. והא דאמרינן אין לו לדיין אלא מה שעיניו רואות, היכא דלא אחזיה כשהוא לח, ולא אידמי ליה כטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:22:4.english: Fading - The appearance of its redness is passing; therefore, he returned to his initial statement and deemed [it] impure. And that which we say, "A judge has only what his eyes see" — [that applies] where it was not shown to him when it was moist, and it did not appear to him as impure.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:23:1.hebrew: בין העמודים - היכא דגרסי, ואע"ג דליכא נהורא כולי האי:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:23:1.english: Between the pillars - Where they study, and even though there is not so much light [there].

Rashi on Niddah 20b:23:2.english: And in the shade of his hand - He places his hand opposite the sun over the blood and casts shade.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:5:1.hebrew: דמרא דארעא דישראל - בקי במראות דם מכל חכמי ארץ ישראל, כדמפרש לקמן. פומבדיתא — אתריה דרב יהודה, בשילהי פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף יז:): סבי דפומבדיתא — רב יהודה ורב עינא:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:5:1.english: Who was the master of the Land of Israel - [He was] more expert in the appearances of blood than all the Sages of the Land of Israel, as [the Gemara] explains below. Pumbedita was Rav Yehuda's place, [as stated] at the end of the first chapter of Sanhedrin (page 17b): "The elders of Pumbedita [are] Rav Yehuda and Rav Eina."

Rashi on Niddah 20b:5:2.english: And he did not examine [it] - Out of respect for Rav Yehuda.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:6:1.english: He smelled it - He smelled it.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:6:2.english: Desire - That she desired her husband and saw the blood because of desire.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:7:1.hebrew: איפרא הורמיז - נכרית היתה, וכן שמה, ואעפ"כ היתה משמרת עצמה מנדות, וקרובה להתגייר, ואף קרבנות היתה שולחת. ולשון יוני: איפרא - חן, כמו ״אפריון נמטייה לרבי שמעון״ (ב"מ דף קיט.):
Rashi on Niddah 20b:7:1.english: Ifra Hormiz - She was a gentile woman, and such was her name; and nevertheless, she would guard herself from [the impurity of] menstruation and was close to converting, and she would even send sacrifices. And in the Greek language, ifra [means] grace, as in: "Let us bring praise [apiryon] to Rabbi Shimon" (Bava Metzia 119a).

Rashi on Niddah 20b:7:2.hebrew: הורמיז - כמו (ב"ב דף עג.) ״הורמיז בר ליליתא״, כלומר: יופי שדים היה לה:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:7:2.english: Hormiz - As in (Bava Batra 73a): "Hormiz son of Lilith"; that is to say, she had the beauty of demons.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:7:3.hebrew: ארחיה כו' - ואע"ג דאמר לעיל רבא לא ידע בדמא, ניסא איתרחיש ליה:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:7:3.english: He smelled it, etc. - And even though [the Gemara] said above that Rava did not know [how to distinguish] blood, a miracle occurred for him.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:8:1.english: He sent her - As a gift.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:8:3.hebrew: מקטלא כלמי - שהורגין עליה כנים. וסברה: ודאי הבין, ומשום הכי שלח לי האי:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:8:3.english: That kills lice - That one kills lice upon it. And she thought: "He certainly understood, and that is why he sent me this."

Rashi on Niddah 20b:8:4.english: Lice - [Means] lice, as we translate [in the Targum]: kinnim [as] kalmeta.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:8:5.english: In the chambers of the heart - You dwell in the chambers of the heart. For [the Hebrew word] mehadarim ["from chambers"] is translated [in the Targum as] mittavnaya. That is to say, all wisdom is found within you.

Rashi on Niddah 20b:9:1.hebrew: לא חזינא - דדילמא אשתני, ואע"ג דמראה דם טהור יש לה, דלמא אי אייתא טיפתא קמייתא הוה מיחזי טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 20b:9:1.english: I do not examine - For perhaps [the blood] changed, and even though it has the appearance of pure blood, perhaps if she had brought the first drop, it would have appeared impure.

Tosafot on Niddah 20b:13:1.hebrew: כל יומא הוה מטהר לי כה"ג - משמע שלא היתה רגילה להראות לרב נחמן בעלה. ושמא לא היה בקי; והא דאמר ר"נ לעיל (נדה דף יט:) בדם הקזה — קבלה היתה בידו. אי נמי, היתה חוששת שמא היה מחמיר על עצמו, להיות לבו נוקפו ופורש, ולא יסמוך על חכמתו. אי נמי, שלא תתגנה בפניו. אבל אין לומר דאסור לראות דמי אשתו, דהא במס' נגעים (פ"ב מ"ה) תנן: כל הנגעים אדם רואה חוץ מנגעי עצמו, ר"מ אומר: אף לא נגעי קרוביו; כל הנדרים אדם מתיר חוץ מנדרי עצמו, ר' יהושע אומר: אף לא נדרי אשתו. ואילו כל הדמים אדם רואה חוץ מדמי אשתו — לא קתני:
Tosafot on Niddah 20b:13:1.english: Every day he would rule [blood] like this to be pure for me - This implies that she was not accustomed to show [her blood] to Rav Nachman, her husband. And perhaps he was not an expert [in discerning blood]; and that which Rav Nachman said above (Niddah 19b) regarding blood from bloodletting — he had a received tradition in hand. Alternatively, she was concerned lest he would be stringent upon himself, such that his heart would smite him [with hesitation] and he would separate [from her], and would not rely on his wisdom. Alternatively, [she did not show him] so that she would not become repulsive in his eyes. However, one cannot say that it is forbidden [for a man] to inspect his wife's blood, for in Tractate Nega'im (2:5) we learned: "A person may inspect all afflictions (nega'im) except his own afflictions; Rabbi Meir says: Even not the afflictions of his relatives. A person may annul all vows except his own vows; Rabbi Yehoshua says: Even not the vows of his wife." Whereas it does not teach: "A person may inspect all blood except the blood of his wife"!

Tosafot on Niddah 20b:19:1.hebrew: אגמריה סמך - לפי הפשט משמע דלכך האמין לדבריה, אבל בענין אחר [פירוש: בלא דבריה] לא היה מתיר, אע"ג דאגמריה סמך. וקשה, דבפ' אלו טרפות (חולין מט.) אמרו גבי ההיא מחטא דאישתכח בסימפונא דכבדא: הונא מר בריה דרב אידי טריף, ורב אחא בר מניומי מכשיר. לכך נראה לפרש, דהשתא הדר ביה משינויא קמא, והיכא דאגמריה סמיך רשאי להתיר, אע"ג דחכם כבר אסר. ויש מקשה על ילתא: היכי עבדה הכי? הא אמרינן בפ"ק דמס' ע"ז (דף ז.): הנשאל לחכם וטימא, לא ישאל לחכם ויטהר! וי"ל, דקפידא לא הויא אשואל אלא אחכם, אבל השואל ישאל כל מה שירצה, דמתוך כך ידקדקו בדבר, ופעמים שהראשון טועה ויצא הדבר לאורה. [ועי' תוס' ע"ז ז. ד"ה הנשאל, ותוס' חולין מד: ד"ה היכי]:
Tosafot on Niddah 20b:19:1.english: He relied on his learning - According to the plain meaning, it implies that for this [reason] he believed her words, but in another manner [meaning: without her words], he would not have permitted [it], even though he relied on his learning. And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] "Elu Terefot" (Chullin 49a), they said regarding that needle which was found in the bronchial tube of the liver: Huna Mar the son of Rav Idi declared [it] treifah, and Rav Acha bar Minyomi declared [it] kosher. Therefore, it seems [correct] to explain that now [the Gemara] retracts from the first resolution, and wherever one relies on his learning, he is permitted to permit [it], even though a Sage has already prohibited [it]. And someone asks regarding Yalta: How could she do this? Behold, we say in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (daf 7a): "One who asked a Sage and he declared [it] impure shall not ask [another] Sage [in order that he] declare it pure"! And it may be answered that the stricture is not upon the questioner, but rather upon the Sage; but the questioner may ask whatever he wishes, for through this they will scrutinize the matter, and sometimes the first [Sage] erred, and the matter will come to light. [And see Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 7a, s.v. Haninsh'al, and Tosafot, Chullin 44b, s.v. Hekhi].

Tosafot on Niddah 20b:4:1.hebrew: והא רבא דידע - רבה גרס, דרבא היה בקי, כדמוכח בסמוך גבי דאפרא הורמיז. ורש"י פירש בסמוך דאיתרחיש ליה ניסא; ואין נראה, דדוקא בסוף הוא דאיתרחיש ליה ניסא, כדמוכח בסמוך:
Tosafot on Niddah 20b:4:1.english: And behold, Rava, who knew - One should read "Rabbah", for Rava was expert [in examining blood], as is proven nearby in the case of Ifra Hormiz. And Rashi explained nearby that a miracle occurred for him; but this does not seem [correct], for it was specifically at the end that a miracle occurred for him, as is proven nearby.

Tosafot on Niddah 20b:9:1.hebrew: טיפתא קמייתא - ושאר חכמים שהיו רואין, לא היו מחמירין כ"כ, או שהיו בקיאין ביותר:
Tosafot on Niddah 20b:9:1.english: The first drop - And the other Sages who would inspect [blood] were not so stringent, or they were exceptionally expert.
